title: Coach's Corner opening segment pose cues
timing: Line-triggered cues. No voice track has been supplied; silent holds are suggestions, not audio timings.
defaultRule: Use each host’s default pose while listening and talk pose for unmarked speech. The cues below override those defaults at the main beats.

cues.label: Opening monitor point
cues.trigger: The YOFHL draft was Saturday, and we’ve got the opening matchups—
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Hold Don’s silent pointing pose through Ron’s introduction.

cues.label: The other thing
cues.trigger: Yeah. And put the thing up.
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Keep the raised arm in place; use the pointing mouth pair.

cues.label: The draft correction
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Small correction; keep Ron’s movement restrained.

cues.label: The draft outburst
cues.trigger: THE DRAFT. That’s what I said.
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Snap into the raised-voice expression.

cues.label: First pick
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Return to the ordinary speaking pose.

cues.label: McKenna correction
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Use the same skeptical pose for Ivar Stenberg.

cues.label: Terrific kid
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Brief shout, then return to ordinary talking for the player discussion.

cues.label: Keeper league
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Let the correction sit for a beat.

cues.label: Keeper outburst
cues.trigger: I KNOW IT’S A KEEPER LEAGUE, RON.
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Hold through I’ve been doing this.

cues.label: Tie adjustment
cues.trigger: [Adjusts tie. Looks down at an empty patch of desk.]
cues.direction: Silent physical beat before Who took him?

cues.label: Who took him
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Return from the tie adjustment into the speaking pose.

cues.label: Jeremy answer
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Use defaults between ordinary back-and-forth lines.

cues.label: Already on him
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Don gives Ron a brief sideways stare.

cues.label: Wilson setup
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Hold Don’s reaction until seventy-sixth.

cues.label: Seventy-sixth
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Use surprise briefly before Don launches into the point.

cues.label: There is your league
cues.trigger: There. There’s your league. Right there.
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Point through the Wilson praise.

cues.label: Good players
cues.trigger: Nylander and Hischier are very good players.
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Calm correction.

cues.label: Did I say
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Use the angry speaking pose through the defensive rant.

cues.label: Good for Eric
cues.trigger: Eric got him. Good for Eric. Smart.
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: A brief approving thumbs-up.

cues.label: Hall Monitors name
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Don turns the deadpan stare toward Ron.

cues.label: Hall Monitors silence
cues.direction: No speaking shake. Let the stare hold before Alright.

cues.label: Alright
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Small delivery, then use the ordinary mouth pairs for the score exchange.

cues.label: Smart correction
cues.trigger: You just said Eric was smart.
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Dry observation.

cues.label: Boston line
cues.trigger: He IS smart. Doesn’t mean he’s winning. You can be smart and lose. I coached Boston.
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Do not overplay the joke before the reaction.

cues.label: Ron looks down
cues.direction: Hold the suppressed smile. Keep Ron still.

cues.label: Do not start
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Return Ron to his default/talk pair for I didn’t say anything.

cues.label: Jagrtown
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Ordinary delivery; Ron uses skeptical-talk for Skellige Sirens.

cues.label: Five games
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Emphasize the shout; Ron’s next correction uses skeptical-talk.

cues.label: What did I say
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Return to ordinary speech for It’s very close.

cues.label: Long pause
cues.direction: Freeze the vacant expression before Paddyville; no mouth cycling.

cues.label: Paddyville
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Resume ordinary mouth pairs for the Pat/Dillon exchange.

cues.label: Sudden callback
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Fast change to pointing; Ron reacts briefly before stating the matchup.

cues.label: One goal
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Repeat on ONE GOAL, RON; Ron uses skeptical-talk for Eighteen assists.

cues.label: Shoot the thing
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Hold the angry frame through the rant.

cues.label: They are winning
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Underplay Ron’s correction.

cues.label: Group chat warning
cues.trigger: I wouldn’t say a WORD in the group chat.
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Hold through Put the phone in a drawer. This pose deliberately faces the audience.

cues.trigger: Carolina’s also ahead of West Texas.

cues.direction: Don returns to his inward-facing default.

cues.label: Hits praise

cues.direction: Ordinary speaking pose.

cues.direction: Use the skeptical pose again for We’re discussing fantasy hockey.

cues.label: Losing at it

cues.direction: Angry emphasis.

cues.label: Until Monday
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Use ordinary pairs through the Thursday trophies exchange.

cues.label: Mic removal
cues.direction: Silent gesture; Ron interrupts before Don leaves.

cues.label: Twenty seconds
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Keep Don holding the mic until his next line.

cues.label: Set lineups
cues.trigger: I want to say one thing. You boys. Set your lineups.
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Direct-to-camera address through the lineup lecture.

cues.label: Don interruption
cues.speaker: ron
cues.direction: Use the stop gesture exactly on the interruption.

cues.label: Bad picks
cues.trigger: BAD PICKS. I said bad picks.
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: A brief defensive recovery.

cues.label: Closing thumbs-up
cues.speaker: don
cues.direction: Finish on the closed smiling thumbs-up after the last word.

cues.label: Final hold
cues.direction: Hold the smile to close the segment.
